content:
Last Friday (21st), during the sentencing of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China case, a police officer took a woman who was queuing to attend the hearing to a police vehicle in the small hours. Police said in response to enquiries that the woman was charged with three offences: "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "obstructing or wilfully resisting a police officer in the execution of his duty" and "with seditious intent".

Around 5am last Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the wait, a plainclothes police officer pointed to a woman in the queue and said her "clothing was suspected of containing a slight element of sedition", and took her away in a police vehicle. While removing the woman, several officers repeatedly told reporters to leave, saying "take you to the press area", and stretched orange cordon tape towards Ying Wa Street. It was only after the woman had boarded the police vehicle that they put the cordon away. On the day, a "court hearing enthusiast" who was queuing near the woman said she was wearing a black T-shirt printed with Japanese characters.

"集誌社" (Feature Media) enquired with the police about the reason for taking the woman away and whether an arrest had been made. Police replied this morning (24th) that during a security operation near the West Kowloon Court on 21 August, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "behaving in a disorderly manner in a public place", "obstructing or wilfully resisting a police officer in the execution of his duty" and "with seditious intent", and was detained for investigation.
